title: MeterReading
description: One reading in response to a NextAction: a multimeter value the person typed or said, a check the product ran on itself (`selftest`, read over Bluetooth or decoded from the status LED's blinks), or a measurement the phone's own sensors took (`phone`). The only kind of evidence that counts as proof (I1, I2). Sent into fusion. `kind` fixes the shape of `value`: voltage_dc -> {volts}; continuity -> {continuity} and pins required; resistance -> {ohms} and pins required; selftest -> {index, ok, transport, value_mv?, state?} and net required; magnetometer -> {delta_uT, state}; audio -> {hz}; flicker -> {hz, depth}; light -> {state on|off|dim}; led -> {state on|off|blinking, color?}, the five sensor kinds with part required. The verdict (`verdict`) is judged against [min, max] in code.

net.description: Net name from the design's electrical reference. Not a harness wire name. Required for continuity, voltage_dc, resistance and selftest; absent on a reading that is about a part.

part.description: The part of the product a phone-sensor reading is about (a motor, a fan, the status LED), in the design's own naming. Required for magnetometer, audio, flicker, light and led.

pins.description: REF.PIN ids probed, in the design's net naming (e.g. J1.1), not harness end names. Required for continuity and resistance; optional for voltage_dc ([probe +, probe -]).

value.description: Exactly the shape that matches kind (see allOf).

condition.description: Operating condition when read. We use it to pick which part of the SPICE [min, max] applies.

expected.description: What RepairOS judged against. volts_min/volts_max come from the reference's expected {min, max}, never from a single expected value.

verdict.description: RepairOS's verdict, computed in code against expected (inside [min - tol, max + tol], tol = 0.25 V or 5 %; under 5 ohm conducts).

source.description: `typed` / `voice`: a person typed or said what a meter showed. `selftest`: the product ran the check on itself and the app read the result over Bluetooth or decoded its blinks through the camera; nobody typed it. `phone`: the phone's own sensor took the measurement. `ble` is DEPRECATED: the app no longer reads third-party Bluetooth meters, no app writes it, and it stays valid only so readings stored before this version still validate.

meter.description: DEPRECATED, only with source `ble`: the third-party meter that produced the reading. No app writes it any more.

mode.description: The mode the meter was in when the value was read.

range.description: The meter's own range label, or "auto".

interval_ms.description: Update interval the app asked the meter for, in milliseconds.

battery_v.description: The meter's battery voltage when read.

read_at.description: When the app received the value from the meter.

raw_text.description: What the user said or typed, before parsing.

continuity.description: True when the meter beeps / reads under 5 ohm.

value_selftest.description: One check of the product's self-test. `index` is the check's place in the product's own list (the plan's self_test.checks maps it to a net). `ok` is the product's own verdict on itself (ok, fail, or unknown when it could not tell); the number is still judged against the design.

value_mv.description: A rail check: the voltage the product measured on itself, in millivolts.

state.description: An output check: whether the product reports the output on.

transport.description: How the app received it: read over Bluetooth, or decoded from the status LED's blinks through the camera.

value_magnetometer.description: The change in the magnetic field the phone felt at the part, in microtesla, against a baseline taken just before with the product off. `current` when the change is at least 5 microtesla and at least 3 times the baseline's own noise.

value_audio.description: The tone the microphone heard from the part (a motor or fan), reduced to its fundamental, in hertz.

value_flicker.description: The strongest brightness oscillation the camera saw: its frequency in hertz and its modulation depth from 0 (steady) to 1 (fully on and off).

value_light.description: Relative brightness of the scene as the camera's exposure reports it, against a baseline taken with the product off. iOS has no public lux sensor, so this is a ratio and never a lux value.

value_led.description: What the camera saw an LED do: lit, dark or blinking, and the hue of its brightest region.

color.description: The hue of the brightest region, as a plain colour word: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink or white.
